page_title: No Magic: Regular Expressions • Russell Cohen

summary.title: No Magic: Regular Expressions
summary.one_liner: You learn how to parse a basic regular expression (., |, +, *, parentheses) into a syntax tree using Scala parser combinators, as the first step toward building a small regex engine.
takeaways: Regular expressions can be represented as a tree of Literal, Or, Concat, Repeat and Plus nodes.
Operator precedence in regex: literals and parentheses bind tightest, then + and *, then concatenation, then |.
Scala's RegexParsers let you write a parser by describing grammar rules, one level per binding strength.
The overall plan is parse to a syntax tree, convert to an NFA, then evaluate the NFA against the input string.
summary.summary: The post is part 1 of a 3-part series on building a basic regular expression engine in under 200 lines of Scala. It specifies a small regex language (., |, +, *, parentheses), outlines a three-phase plan (parse to a syntax tree, convert to an NFA, evaluate), and notes that the approach resembles Ken Thompson's 1968 method and non-backtracking engines like RE2. The main body shows the case classes for the tree and walks through a Scala parser-combinator implementation that handles operator precedence across four binding levels.
